Currently we will not broadcast these changes but I wanted to merge today when I wake up the PR to broadcast at the fork The thing is the subtlety between head state and wall clock. I'll go with wall clock is after the fork and I'm hoping all clients do this. Head state may happen before, so it's safe that other clients that don't agree on when to start accepting will take our changes, but also it may mean that we will lose the race for inclusion in the pool we dont need to worry about the head state since the fork version has been changed to the genesis fork version, it doesn't matter we can still verify change messages in gossip if the head state is in bellatrix We do need to worry, the issue here is when do clients will start accepting these changes into their pools instead of ignoring why would they ignore them ? Because that's what the spec says There's still discussion as to what to do, I'm on the camp that we should ignore and accept only at wall clock at The fork. And also that we should broadcast all local changes at the fork (again wall clock) ``` Ignore signed_bls_to_execution_change message before CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH ``` This is fine it just means if your local clock is before the fork epoch you ignore it Yes But if clients decide to implement head state instead of wall clock, there may be a subtlety with optimizations that advance and process the slot before the wall clock And if clients also decide to broadcast right after Epoch transition instead of wall clock, then those clients will fill their pools before we broadcast our local changes. So I think it's better to agree on one event to all behave the same way I think the spec is clear here in that it is referring to wall clock, rather than the head state If clients are broadcasting, then following the wall clock makes much more sense.
